gen-gf-gugi-gf-chivo: Distinctive is the right word for Gugi, whose strokes keep one width and whose terminals are cut open. Chivo is the sans underneath, with a lowercase packed up toward the caps and daylight in every curve.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-chocolate-classical-sans: Rounded rods, single weight, terminals cut open: that's Gugi. Chocolate Classical Sans is the plain sans, a sizable lowercase drawn with a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-comme: Bold from the first glance, Gugi cuts its terminals open and lets no downstroke swell. And Comme, the plain sans below, is smooth to read, its lowercase bodies filling most of the height.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-duru-sans: Gugi opens the pair with identical bar thickness across every line, its terminals cut open. Duru Sans then takes over as a modern sans, its small letters wide-mouthed and its ascenders barely showing.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-fresca: Gugi leads with lowercase nearly reaching the capitals and terminals cut open, so its counters flow outward. Fresca keeps every counter linked to the space outside, with no thinning.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-funnel-sans: Loud, round and cut open at the terminals, Gugi meets Funnel Sans, a sans whose stroke widths stay put. Gugi is happiest up in the heading, where its curves can be seen.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-gafata: Reading Gafata means a band of letters with short stalks above and a wide-eyed lowercase e. Gafata, the plain sans, sits against Gugi, whose round letters keep walls matching the straight ones.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-geist: Bold letters with cut-open terminals and curves that match the stems: that's Gugi. Geist, the sans-serif body, keeps a quiet level beat, so words settle into solid blocks rather than skylines down a whole page of text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-gidole: Loud and distinctive, Gugi cuts its terminals open and matches its curves to its stems. Gidole, a sans-serif, draws every stroke with neon-tube consistency, its terminals held apart like scissor blades.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-golos-text: Approachable is the first word for Golos Text, a sans-serif whose x-height fills the line and whose s is widely parted. Shrink Gugi, though, and its bold cut-open terminals lose their punch.
